findings: Saved state contains entered approve-usdc and signed submission-unknown record under reconcile-only policy. No private signed bytes or keys were printed.

approve-usdc-first.log unresolved result lacks transactionHash. The execute catch in onceAztecOperation produces exactly that shape; reconcileRollingEthereum includes record.hash in every unresolved result. Thus this is an execution exception at or after signed-state persistence, not merely a successful broadcast followed by receipt-null reconciliation.

Durable-state presence alone does not prove the original network send occurred: persistence may have thrown after writing, the explicit broadcast guard may have thrown, or ethers broadcast may have rejected. Exact original exception was discarded.

Installed ethers broadcastTransaction concurrently awaits getBlockNumber, sendRawTransaction and getNetwork, then verifies the returned hash. A read-side error can therefore reject the combined call without establishing whether send was accepted.
Strict transport rejects non200 responses and oversized bodies; no original HTTP/RPC code is retained. Do not assert429, fee rejection or expiry as established cause.

PublicNode.result: HTTP403 for receipt/transaction/nonce reads; no independent transaction visibility conclusion

recommendation: Keep original hash/nonce and fixed plan reconcile-only; block successor nonce. The smallest useful local controlled check is failure-shape coverage for persistence and each ethers broadcast dependency, with future original-operation diagnostics restricted to finite phase/HTTP/RPC code. It cannot recover the historical error and must not resend this transaction. Further read-only hash receipt queries may establish later inclusion; absence is not resend authority.
